name: CapCut Auto Subject And Sticker Tracking
use_when: A speaker's face, body, or hand needs to stay framed using CapCut's built-in tracking.
A sticker, arrow, label, or graphic should follow a person or object for a short emphasis beat.
The tracked target remains visible and distinct across the affected range.
avoid_when: The subject turns away, leaves frame, is heavily occluded, or blends into the background.
Tracking drift would cover captions, faces, proof, UI, products, or action.
The app/platform lacks the needed tracking feature for the current device.
Manual keyframes would be more reliable for a short or simple move.

timeline_pattern.pattern: choose_clip_or_sticker -> place_initial_position -> choose_face_body_hand_or_object_target -> start_tracking -> preview_drift -> adjust_or_keyframe_fix -> caption_safe_review
timeline_pattern.target_rule: Choose the most stable visible feature: face when it stays front-facing, body when full-body motion matters, hand only when the hand remains clear.
timeline_pattern.sticker_rule: Place the sticker in its desired final relation to the subject before starting tracking.
timeline_pattern.device_rule: If tracking is unavailable on one device, use another supported device or manual keyframes.
timeline_pattern.reject_rule: Reject or shorten the tracking section when the tracker loses the target.

motion.rule: Tracking should guide attention without turning the crop or sticker into the main distraction.

keyframe_values.target_visibility: Keep the tracked feature visible through the whole tracking range.
keyframe_values.sticker_offset: Set the sticker offset before tracking, such as above the head or pointing to the product.
keyframe_values.review_range: Scrub the full tracked section after generation and fix drift with manual keyframes or shorter ranges.
keyframe_values.safe_crop: If tracking reframes the clip, preserve face, hands, captions, proof, and action.

sound.rule: Add a small pop or tick only if the sticker/arrow entrance is a real emphasis beat.

captions.rule: Tracked stickers and reframed crops must not enter caption safe areas unless captions are intentionally moved or suppressed.

color.rule: Sticker or arrow colors should contrast with the background without feeling unrelated to the style pack.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use external tracking data if available; otherwise approximate with manually keyframed overlay x/y positions and crop transforms.
implementation.remotion: Store trackingTarget, targetType, stickerOffset, generatedTrackPoints, driftFixFrames, and safeRegions.
implementation.blender: Use motion tracking or object tracking for attached graphics, then review occlusion and drift across the full range.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: On supported mobile devices, use Camera Tracking for face/body/hand or Tracking on a sticker/overlay, place the tracking circle on the target, start tracking, then preview and shorten/fix drift.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use mask tracking, position keyframes, or send to After Effects for point tracking/rotoscoping when the graphic must follow a moving feature.

common_mistakes: Tracking a face that turns out of frame and expecting the app to recover.
Placing a sticker before deciding its final relationship to the subject.
Accepting drift because the first frame looked correct.
Letting a tracked sticker cover captions or the subject's expression.
Assuming every CapCut device version exposes the same tracking controls.
qc: Does the tracked target stay visible through the full range?
Does the crop or sticker drift, jitter, or jump?
Does the sticker point to a real feature and clear before it becomes clutter?
Do captions, faces, proof, UI, products, and action remain safe?
Is manual keyframing better for this shot?
